segments.name: e3-open

params.title: Shielding and unshielding
params.line: Zodl was called Zashi in older guides

narration: By the end of this video, your ZEC will be shielded. You will also know when to unshield and what it shows.

segments.name: e3-sees
narration: First, what does the blockchain see? The blockchain is a public record of payments. Anyone can look at it.
A transparent payment is like a postcard. Anyone can read who sent it, who got it and how much.
A shielded payment is like a sealed letter. The amount, the sender and the receiver are encrypted. Only the people in the payment can read it.

segments.name: e3-shield

params.label: Diagram, not the app
params.definition: Shielding: moving your own ZEC from transparent to shielded

narration: Shielding means moving your own ZEC from transparent to shielded.
When ZEC lands at your transparent address, Zodl shows Unshielded Balance. Tap Shield.
If a sheet opens, tap Shield again. When Zodl shows Shielded!, you are done.

segments.name: e3-ironwood

params.label: Illustration
params.line: If Zodl asks you to migrate, that is a normal upgrade

narration: Your shielded ZEC goes into Ironwood, the newest shielded pool. You do not have to do anything.
If Zodl asks you to migrate to Ironwood, that is a normal upgrade, your ZEC stays shielded.

segments.name: e3-unshield

params.label: Diagram
params.chip: tex1: Zodl does the two steps for you

narration: Unshielding is the opposite. You send ZEC from your shielded balance to a transparent address.
You only need it when you must pay an address that starts with t1 or tex1. Some exchanges use tex1 addresses for deposits.
When you unshield, the amount and that address are public. You cannot add a note. For a tex1 address, Zodl does the two steps for you.

segments.name: e3-checker

params.banner: Nothing you paste leaves your browser

narration: Not sure what an address is? Paste it into the address checker on the site.
Your Zodl u1 address is shielded. A t1 or tex1 address is transparent. Nothing you paste leaves your browser.

segments.name: e3-end
narration: Tick Shielding and Unshielding. Next, episode 4: your first shielded payment.

upload.title: Shielding and unshielding | Zero to Shielded 3
upload.description:
Shield your ZEC in Zodl so your balance is private. Then learn when to unshield and what it shows. This is episode 3 of Zero to Shielded.

Watch the series and tick your progress: https://zero-to-shielded.vercel.app

In this episode:
- What the blockchain sees. A transparent payment is like a postcard: anyone can read who sent it, who got it and how much. A shielded payment is like a sealed letter: only the people in the payment can read it.
- Shielding means moving your own ZEC from transparent to shielded. When Zodl shows Unshielded Balance, tap Shield.
- Your shielded ZEC goes into Ironwood, the newest shielded pool. If Zodl asks you to migrate to Ironwood, that is a normal upgrade, your ZEC stays shielded.
- Unshielding means sending ZEC from your shielded balance to a transparent address. You only need it when you must pay an address that starts with t1 or tex1. The amount and that address are public and you cannot add a note.
- Not sure what an address is? Paste it into the address checker on the site. Nothing you paste leaves your browser.

Chapters:
{chapters}

Wallet steps are shown as labelled step diagrams with the exact button names from the Zodl app, not as drawings of the app. Every fact is sourced in docs/FACTS.md. No recovery phrase appears on screen.

Zodl was called Zashi in older guides.

Zodl: https://zodl.com/
Zodl support: https://support.zodl.com/

Video, narration and script: CC BY-ND 4.0. Repost with credit, no edits.

Scripts, narration and editing were produced with AI assistance (Kiro). Narration is a synthesised voice (Kokoro, Apache-2.0). Music is original and generated in code.
